newsitem.title: USA: Stone won't pay preferred dividend.
newsitem.headline: Stone won't pay preferred dividend.

text.p: Stone Container Corp said Wednesday it will skip payment of a preferred stock dividend in May 1997 because of a shortfall in its dividend pool.

"It's a covenant issue, not a cash problem," Roger Stone, chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters. He said the paper company's covenants stipulate it cannot pay a dividend unless there is an adequate dividend pool, which is calculated by earnings.
In 1996, Stone reported a loss of $1.35 per share compared to a year-earlier profit of $2.24 per share. On January 27, its board eliminated the common stock dividend.

Stone said his company has omitted payment of a preferred dividend once before. "The company has plenty of liquidity and the ability to pay the small (preferred) dividend ($2 million), but we can't under our covenant," he noted.
Earlier Wednesday, Standard & Poor's lowered its preferred stock rating of Stone to CCC from single-B.
Roger Stone said the preferred dividend would be considered again in succeeding quarters.
